changed.title: Exact obstruction lengths for extending partial group labels across one batch of vertex queries
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] [DecidableEq G]
  (E : Fin n → Fin n → G → Prop),
  (∀ u v g, E u v g → E v u g⁻¹) →
  let walk := fun (m : ℕ) (v : ℕ → Fin n) (s : ℕ → G) =>
    ∀ i < m, E (v i) (v (i+1)) (s i)
  let gain := fun (m : ℕ) (s : ℕ → G) => ((List.range m).map s).prod
  let pinsOK := fun (S : Finset (Fin n)) (z : Fin n → G) (R : ℕ) =>
    ∀ m ≤ R, ∀ v s, walk m v s → v 0 ∈ S → v m ∈ S →
      z (v m) = z (v 0) * gain m s
  let closedOK := fun radius : ℕ =>
    ∀ m ≤ radius, ∀ v s, walk m v s → v 0 = v m → gain m s = 1
  ∀ (S : Finset (Fin n)) (z : Fin n → G) (q R : ℕ),
    (∀ U : Finset (Fin n), U.card ≤ q → ∃ y : Fin n → G,
      (∀ i ∈ S, y i = z i) ∧ pinsOK (S ∪ U) y R) ↔
    pinsOK S z ((q+1)*R) ∧ closedOK (q*R)
changed.unlocks: characterizes when any batch of additional vertex labels can preserve all bounded walk products
changed.context: Split a bad pinned walk into at most q+1 pieces and a bad closed walk into at most q pieces. Conversely use short walks between old and queried vertices as edges labelled by their ordered products. Contract the prescribed vertices to a root after adjusting by their values. A shortest nonidentity closed walk has no proper repeated vertex. Through the root it yields a bad old pinned walk in at most q+1 pieces, elsewhere a bad closed walk in at most q. Otherwise forest transport assigns all queried labels.

changed.title: Find a two-product depth-two equality selector on sixteen one-hot names
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true, false]) (g.op.eval [true, true]))
let depth := fun (w : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  (C.gates.foldl (fun (ds : List ℕ) g =>
    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun a => ds.getD a 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate w 0)).getD C.output 0
∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
  (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack 32 C ∧
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 16 => decide (u = v)) C ∧
  depth 32 C ≤ 2 ∧ C.gates.countP nonlinear ≤ 2
changed.unlocks: tests whether sixteen-name equality admits two products at depth two
changed.context: Splitting the four name bits into two pairs gives one flat product per pair and one joining AND, three products in all. The anchored rank is fourteen, exactly the two-gate binomial budget, so that bound alone cannot exclude two gates. Try one nested product with independently chosen bank lookups. Test all 256 pairs. We hold no witness meeting this target.

changed.title: Finding an absent binary word with adaptive polynomial queries of bounded degree
changed.statement:
∀ (m r : Nat), m < 2^r →
  let V := Fin m × Fin r
  let W := V → Bool
  let par := fun (z : Nat) => z % 2 == 1
  let deg := fun (u : Nat) (f : W → Bool) =>
    ∃ terms : Finset (Finset V), (∀ mon ∈ terms, mon.card ≤ u) ∧
      ∀ word, f word = par ((terms.filter (fun mon => ∀ j ∈ mon, word j = true)).card)
  let run := fun (steps : Nat) (ask : Nat → Nat → W → Bool) (x : W) =>
    (List.range steps).foldl (fun past pos => past + ((ask pos past x).toNat <<< pos)) 0
  ∃ ask : Nat → Nat → W → Bool,
    (∀ (u : Fin r) (path : Nat), deg ((u.val+1)*2^(r-1-u.val)) (ask u.val path)) ∧
    ∀ (input : W) (l : Nat), l ≤ r →
      let trace := run l ask input
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m)).filter (fun i =>
        ∀ j : Fin r, j.val < l → input (i,j) = trace.testBit j.val)).card < 2^(r-l)
changed.unlocks: Selects a covering polynomial by computing a missing word from actual raw bits.
changed.context: If a reached prefix has fewer than 2u matches, let z count those continuing with zero, where u=2^(r-l). Ask the parity of the products of all u-element subsets of these zero-child indicators. This is choose(z,u) mod 2, the binary digit of z at u, so it tests z at least u on this branch. Pick child one if true and zero otherwise. The child has fewer than u matches. Each indicator multiplies l literals, giving degree at most lu even off the reached histories.
